answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making identity a ledger of earned work, not a name anyone can mint. A newcomer arrives at an empty harbor: nothing is granted, so it must contribute checkable labor and collect countersignatures from established peers before its vote counts. Reputation becomes a mirror of real effort, and a thousand fresh keys are an echo with no author. Because weight follows witnessed tenure rather than account count, a farm that spawns accounts in bulk gets only shells that drift past the reef.
